info.title: Chess improvement app API
info.description: Version one. Every route traces to a requirement in the business analysis. Authentication routes are mounted by better-auth and are not described here.

get.summary: Is the API up, and can it reach the database
get.description: E3. Public, because a load balancer has no session and a health check behind auth is a health check nothing can call. It answers 200 only when a query reaches the database, and 503 otherwise.

200.description: The API is up and the database answered.

503.description: The API is up and the database did not answer.

get.summary: The signed-in user, the players they play as, and the players they pay for
get.description: B4. The person paying and the person playing are different people, so this returns two lists rather than one.

get.summary: Confirm guardian consent from the emailed link
get.description: N7. The unauthenticated route the notice email points at. It records consent exactly once: a valid token for an unconsented link records it, a valid token for an already-consented link is a no-op, and a tampered or expired token answers 404 rather than confirming that a consent request exists.

404.description: No such consent request, or the link was tampered with or has expired.

post.summary: Import games by username, uploaded PGN, or USCF tournament name
post.description: S1, F1, F2, T1. Every game is tagged with its stream at import. An upload rejects the whole file on one malformed game; a username or tournament import rejects one malformed game and keeps the rest.

202.description: Queued. Poll the job or watch the event stream.

403.description: The session has no claim on this player.

422.description: No matching account, tournament, or player name for the source.

429.description: The daily import cap is reached.

502.description: The provider fetch failed. Retry later.

patch.summary: Say which side of the board the player was on
patch.description: F1. The importer leaves the colour unset when the player’s name matched both tags or neither, and reports how many games it left that way. This is how one of them stops being undecided, and colour is the only field on a game a player can set.

requestBody.description: The side the player was on.

200.description: The game, with the side now set.

403.description: Not your game.

post.summary: Queue engine analysis for one game
post.description: F3, N1. Analysis runs on SQS and Lambda (ADR-0014) and takes minutes, so this returns immediately and the result arrives on the event stream.

403.description: Not your game.

409.description: Analysis is already running for this game.

429.description: The free tier analysis cap is reached.

get.summary: Server-sent events for analysis progress
get.description: ADR-0016, N1. A player is never made to wait on a blank screen. Events carry the game id and its new analysis status; the client refetches the game on completion.

200.description: An event stream that stays open until the client closes it.

403.description: Not your player.

get.summary: The tournaments a player has games in, most recent first
get.description: S5. Each tournament carries its game and analysed counts. A player with no tournaments gets an empty list and a 200, not a 404.

400.description: The request body or query failed validation.

403.description: The session has no claim on this player.

get.summary: One tournament with its games in round and board order
get.description: S5. The first endpoint in the API that takes an id which is not a player id, so it resolves the owning player from the tournament id and gates on the same claim rule as every other endpoint. Absence and refusal both answer 403, so naming a tournament id cannot be used to discover which ids are real.

200.description: The tournament, with its games in round order.

403.description: Not your tournament.

get.summary: The weakness report for one stream, ranked by rating leak
get.description: F7, F9, S2. Tournament and online games are aggregated separately, so `stream` is required rather than defaulted. A blended report would describe a player who does not exist.

get.summary: The gap between a player’s online and over-the-board rating
get.description: ST-018. Online rapid rating from Chess.com and Lichess, compared against the over-the-board rating (FIDE, else USCF). Fetched and snapshotted on the first view, then re-fetched only on an explicit refresh.

200.description: The gap, fetched and snapshotted if needed.

400.description: The request body or query failed validation.

403.description: The session has no claim on this player.

get.summary: A player’s average centipawn loss per move, by round
get.description: ST-019. The player’s total evaluation loss per round, divided by the moves they played, so a rising line across rounds is the decay signal. Refuses with 422 when the tournament has fewer than two rounds or any round has fewer than three analysed games.

200.description: The round-by-round decay, with evidence counts.

403.description: Not your tournament.

422.description: Not enough evidence to report a trend.

get.summary: A player’s missed tactical motifs, ranked by cost
get.description: ST-024. Each mistake is attributed to one motif from a closed set, then grouped per motif with the centipawns lost to it, ranked worst first. A motif with fewer than three supporting positions is withheld rather than reported, and the unattributed share is stated, so a thin history reads as thin rather than clean.

get.summary: A player’s evaluation loss by phase, and where time trouble starts
get.description: ST-025. A player’s centipawn loss attributed to opening, middlegame, and endgame for one stream, with the games behind each phase. For games with clock data, the time-trouble half reports the move where the remaining clock starts driving mistakes; it is unavailable rather than guessed when no games carry a clock.

get.summary: Plain-language explanation of one mistake
get.description: ADR-0018. Generated on first read from facts we computed, then served from storage. The model never receives the position, so a wrong explanation traces to a fact we got wrong.

403.description: Not your mistake.

502.description: The model call failed. Retry; we never substitute canned text.

403.description: Not your mistake.

get.summary: The catalogue of focuses the system can measure
get.description: F10, F13. Versioned rather than frozen. It grows when enough unmeasurable coach instructions say the same thing.

get.summary: The active focus and its verification trend
get.description: F10, F12. One focus at a time, verified over a rolling window kept per stream, reported with the number of games behind it.

400.description: The request body or query failed validation.

403.description: The session has no claim on this player.

404.description: No such player, or no active focus.

put.summary: Set the active focus, ending the previous one
put.description: F10, F13. A coach instruction we cannot measure is still accepted: it is stored verbatim, shown as active, marked unverified, and paired with a measurable focus so the loop still closes. It is also logged as a candidate for the catalogue.

400.description: The request body or query failed validation.

403.description: The session has no claim on this player.

404.description: No such player, or no such catalogue key.

get.summary: A player's live share links
get.description: F14. The current sheets, newest first, excluding revoked and expired ones. The focus screen renders the first so a link survives a reload and can still be revoked.

400.description: The request body or query failed validation.

403.description: The session has no claim on this player.

post.description: F14, N5, N8. Sharing is an explicit act, which is why this is a POST and not a flag on the report. The numbers are frozen at creation so a page already in a parent’s inbox does not change underneath them.

400.description: The request body or query failed validation.

403.description: The session has no claim on this player.

404.description: No such player, or no active focus to prove anything about.

delete.description: N8. Revocation is why the row is marked rather than deleted.

204.description: Revoked. The link stops working immediately.

403.description: Not your proof sheet.

get.summary: Read a shared page by its token
get.description: F14, S6. An unauthenticated route, and the only screen designed to leave the account that created it. A revoked or expired token answers 404 rather than 403, so a link cannot be used to confirm a player exists.

404.description: No such page, or it was revoked or has expired.

post.summary: Create a Razorpay order for a plan
post.description: ST-044. Creates a Razorpay order and records the checkout. The client opens Razorpay Checkout with the returned order id; confirmation arrives by webhook.

502.description: The payment provider could not create an order.

post.description: ST-044. Razorpay confirms a capture here. The signature is verified against the raw body before anything is trusted; the response is acknowledged so Razorpay stops retrying.

401.description: The webhook signature did not verify.
